subject: ventures/wall-framing-takeoff
auditor: agent session (Claude), round 78, see run record
professional: a lead framer / framing estimator for residential wood-frame work (stud, opening, plate and order arithmetic), plus, for the modules added since r4, a licensed plumber or plumbing engineer who sizes domestic water supply (design flow per branch, friction loss, residual pressure at the worst fixture) and a concrete flatwork contractor laying out slab control joints. Each checks first: that every fixture branch carries at least the flow of the fixture it feeds and the worst fixture keeps its minimum pressure; that joint spacing is 24 to 36 times the thickness with panels no longer than 1.5 times their width; that kings, jacks, headers and cripples are cut right.

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against sources the author did not write. (1) Water supply, Hunter demand: ran sizeSupply(EXAMPLE) (main 12.2 gpm, riser 7, bath-1 5, bath-2 5, kitchen-laundry 6.2) and recomputed every branch with my own Python brute force over every on/off pattern (2^11 for the main): 12.2 / 7.0 / 5.0 / 5.0 / 6.2, identical. Applied the same 99% binomial rule to Hunter's 1940 (NBS BMS65) flush-valve parameters (27 gpm, 9 s per 300 s, p = 0.03): 100 valves (1000 fixture units) gives 8 x 27 = 216 gpm and 200 flush tanks (4 gpm, p = 0.2) 216 gpm, close to the 1000-WSFU row of IPC Table E103.3(3) (about 208 to 210 gpm, recalled; codes.iccsafe.org is not reachable from this session). (2) Pipe loss: my own Colebrook by bisection with the textbook kinematic viscosity at 60 F (1.217e-5 ft^2/s) and ASTM B88 type L bores (0.545 / 0.785 / 1.025 in = OD minus two walls, identical to the tool): 12.2 gpm in 1 in L gives 4.744 ft/s, f 0.0231, 4.09 psi/100 ft against the tool's 4.744 / 0.02304 / 4.085; 7 gpm in 3/4 L 5.48 vs 5.466; 5 gpm in 1/2 L 17.27 vs 17.234 (within 0.3%, the gap is the viscosity fit); Hazen-Williams C=150 is 6 to 8% lower, as expected. (3) Slab control joints against ACI 302.1R (joints at 24 to 36 times thickness, panel aspect at most 1.5, saw-cut depth a quarter of the thickness) and the common 15 ft cap: 144x144x4 -> 4 panels of 72 in, 24 ft of cut, 1 in deep; 360x144x5 -> 150 in limit, 3 panels 120x144, 24 ft; 156x48x4 walkway -> 2 panels would be 78x48 (1.625:1) so 3 panels 52x48, 8 ft; 480x480x6 -> 9 panels 160 in, 160 ft; all equal to the tool. (4) Outlet cable holes: 20 ft 2x4 wall at 16 o.c., boxes snapped to 62.125 and 177.875 in; studs whose centres lie between the boxes (64, 80, ... 176) = 8 holes, 16 for an unsheathed two-face wall; tool 8 and 16. 3/4 in hole in a 2x4 leaves 1.375 in to each edge, over NEC 300.4(A)(1)'s 1-1/4 in. (5) Framing re-run of r4's plan: kings at 27, 67-1/2, 97, 221-1/2, jacks 81, headers 123 and 39, cripples 31-1/2 and 6-1/8, 3/8 in door gap: unchanged and right. WRONG: any fixture branch whose fixtures have busy fraction p <= 0.01 gets a 99% design flow of 0 gpm, zero friction loss and a pass. Ran a 300 ft 1/2 in PEX branch to one shower (p 0.0093) on 40 psi: tool says 'design 0 gpm, 39.6 psi at the end ... Every fixture keeps at least 20 psi'; when that shower runs at 2.5 gpm the branch loses 27.2 psi (tool's own pipeFlow) and the fixture gets about 12.4 psi. A single toilet branch at p = 0.01 (the order of magnitude published modern-use probabilities take) gets main 0 / branch 0 gpm; at p = 0.0101 it gets 3 gpm. Hunter's own fixture-unit curve and IPC Table E103.3(3) never go below one fixture's flow (1 WSFU = 3 gpm). A wrong pass verdict a plumber would act on, so 2.

evidence.verification: Full suite node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture: 1212 tests, 1211 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, 25 s wall. Targeted: supplysize, slab, slab-fuzz, electrical, engine, headers, mutation-sweep, stock-memo, more-tools, schedule: 163 pass. Seven seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: supply fittings length dropped from loss (caught), elevation sign flipped (caught), default quantile 0.99 -> 0.98 (caught), quantile boundary >= -> > (SURVIVED; near-equivalent, changes output only on an exact tie), slab Math.ceil -> Math.round panel count (caught), slab maxAspect 1.5 -> 2 (caught), electrical holes per face dropped (SURVIVED the whole suite: the only cable-hole test is single-face and recomputes the tool's own filter). r4's jack mutant (engine.mjs:402) now fails 2 tests in the full suite (r4: 1). No test covers a low-p single-fixture branch, which is how the 0 gpm defect got through. 5 of 7 caught; 3.

The supply page's disclaimer reuses framing boilerplate ('not checked against any span table ... property line'). Good new code, unchanged monoliths: 2.
evidence.claims: Supply page and README: 'Hunter's rule computed exactly' (true: brute force matches), 'Not the IPC/UPC fixture-unit tables, which an inspector checks' (stated on page footer and README), normal-approximation finding '10.76 gpm vs exact 12.2' (tool normalGpm 10.7588, demand 12.2: backed), FAQ '27.2 gpm all on, 8.1 ft/s in 3/4 in' (27.2 and 12.2/448.831/0.003361 = 8.09: backed). Slab README '144 x 144 x 4: 4 panels of 72 in, 24 ft, 1 in deep': backed. Disclaimer on the supply page (No warranty, not engineering advice, have a licensed plumber size it). Overstated: the page's results line 'Every fixture keeps at least N psi' is printed for a branch sized at 0 gpm (see correctness); README:154 still says 1,039 tests across 124 files (now 1212). llms.txt lists the supply page; served copy clean. 3 with those two notes.
evidence.fitness: Walked a plumber's job: typed a two-bath house (the example), got per-run sizes, velocities, losses and end pressures in one pass, with the all-on and normal flows beside the design flow; a plumber could use it to check a layout before the code-table sizing. Walked the slab job: dimensions in, panel count, cut length and depth out. Framer's job unchanged from r4 and now with a wide-opening note. Friction: supply has no CLI, its p values are the user's guess (the example's are 5 to 15 times the busy fractions modern demand studies publish), and a user who types low p values gets 0 gpm branches that pass.
evidence.domain: Framing: IRC R602 opening framing and R311.7 stairs as r4; the wide-opening default now gets a per-opening note (engine.mjs:646). Slab joints match ACI 302.1R / ACI 360R practice (24-36 x thickness, aspect <= 1.5, 1/4-depth saw cut; the 6 to 18 h timing is looser than ACI's usual 'as soon as it can be cut without ravelling'). Supply: Hunter's binomial at the 99th percentile is the method behind the IPC/UPC tables and the IAPMO Water Demand Calculator; Darcy/Colebrook is the textbook loss. Departures: no floor at the largest fixture flow on a branch (Hunter's curve and the code tables start at one fixture's flow), a single velocity limit for hot and cold (CDA guidance is lower for hot water), and no hot/cold split. The binomial departure is a high defect but confined to low p; the method is otherwise sound, so 3.

defects.what: A pipe run whose fixtures have busy fraction p <= 0.01 gets a 99% design flow of 0 gpm, zero friction loss and a pass: a 300 ft 1/2 in PEX branch to one shower (p 0.0093) on 40 psi prints 'design 0 gpm ... 39.6 psi at the end' and 'Every fixture keeps at least 20 psi', while the shower running at 2.5 gpm loses 27.2 psi and gets about 12.4 psi. A lone toilet at p = 0.01 sizes the whole system for 0 gpm. Hunter's fixture-unit curve and IPC Table E103.3(3) never fall below one fixture's flow; the engine needs a floor at the largest fixture flow fed (or a refusal/warning) and a test with low p.
No test exercises a branch whose 99% flow rounds to zero (single fixture with p <= 0.01); the brute-force and Monte Carlo tests use the example's high p values, so the 0 gpm pass went unseen.
Dropping the per-face multiplier on cable holes survives the whole suite: the only cable-hole test is single-face and recomputes the tool's own stud filter, though its name says 'per face'.
Supply sizing applies one velocity limit (default 8 ft/s) to every run and has no hot/cold split, while copper guidance holds hot water lower (about 5 ft/s); the page does not say so.
r4 defect 2, partly improved: the jack-length mutant now fails 2 tests in the full suite (r4: 1 of 143 in the subset), still a thin guard on core opening geometry.
r4 defect 3, still open: no default or example header span table; header size is entirely the user's input.
r4 defect 4, still open: README says 1,039 tests across 124 files (2026-11-07); the suite is 1212 tests today. README is 591 lines of very long bullets.
r4 defect 5, still open: layoutGable repeats layoutWall's opening-framing loop (a studAt helper now covers part of it); engine.mjs grew to 1718 lines, cli.mjs to 692.

verdict: Fifth audit of the flagship. The new Hunter's-rule water sizing is mostly sound: each branch's 99% flow matches my brute-force enumeration exactly, Hunter's 1940 flush-valve and flush-tank parameters give about 216 gpm at 1000 fixture units, close to the code table, and Darcy/Colebrook loss is within 0.3% of my own solver. Slab joint layouts match ACI 302.1R practice, outlet cable-hole counts match a hand count, and the r4 framing numbers still recompute. But any branch whose fixtures each have p <= 0.01 is sized for 0 gpm and reported as passing the pressure check (a 300 ft 1/2 in PEX shower branch shows 39.6 psi where about 12.4 psi arrives), a wrong pass a plumber would act on. So correctness drops to 2 and the subject misses the bar this round (r4: met it). Suite 1211/1212 pass, 5 of 7 new mutants are caught. Of the r4 defects, the wide-opening note is fixed (engine.mjs:646), the single-test jack guard is slightly better (2 tests), and the span table, the stale README count and the duplicated gable loop remain open. Scores are before any fix.
